answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 40% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the ocean calculation reruns each epoch, the wharf weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the terrace settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 139 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 19 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
